item.title: Quantum Key Distribution with Entanglement-Swapped Photons from a Quantum Emitter
item.description:
Pay dirt new result — Secret key distribution implemented using entanglement-swapped photons from a GaAs quantum dot, yielding an estimated secure key rate of 1×10−3 bit at optimal 30 ps BSM temporal post-selection.

Grade 0.495 · 3.3σ above the day's baseline · matched “cavity QED, atom-photon interfaces and quantum networks” · Michele B. Rota, Francesco Basso Basset, Alessandro Laneve, Francesco Salusti, Nicolas Claro-Rodriguez, Giuseppe Ronco, Mattia Beccaceci, Tobias M. Krieger, Quirin Buchinger, Saimon F. Covre da Silva, Sandra Stroj, Mariia Gumberidze, Vladyslav Usenko, Sven Höfling, Tobias Huber-Loyola, Mario A. Usuga Castaneda, Armando Rastelli, Klaus D. Jöns, Rinaldo Trotta

Figure

Quantum bit error rate (QBER) and Bell parameter S plotted against BSM coincidence time window. Shows the trade-off where narrower time windows reduce error and push S above the classical limit of 2.

Asks

Can correlated photons generated from a deterministic quantum emitter and distributed via all-photonic entanglement swapping support secure quantum key distribution?

But

Asymptotic limit. Employs single-emitter temporal multiplexing rather than independent remote quantum dots; requires high temporal filtering (30 ps) to overcome distinguishability limits.

Tools

strain-tuned GaAs/AlGaAs quantum dot in circular Bragg resonator · resonant two-photon excitation (biexciton-exciton cascade) · linear optics Bell state measurement (BSM) · asymmetric source-independent Ekert QKD protocol · high-resolution temporal post-selection

Abstract

Quantum key distribution (QKD) is a fundamental functionality of quantum networks. Extending its range requires quantum repeaters, a technology still under development and not yet demonstrated in combination with quantum cryptographic protocols. Here, we address the elementary operation of a viable quantum repeater scheme by evaluating whether correlated photons distributed via entanglement swapping can support secret key distribution. We employ a state-of-the-art deterministic photon source based on a strain-tuned GaAs quantum dot embedded in a photonic cavity and implement a source-independent QKD protocol between two nodes using entanglement-swapped photons. We benchmark the system and present how high-resolution temporal post-selection can enable secure key exchange, with further rate improvements expected through realistic device and protocol optimizations. Due to its compatibility with a wide range of quantum memory platforms, our approach represents a significant step towards long-distance quantum-safe communication.

item.title: Gap-Protected Heisenberg-Limited Squeezing with Locally Interacting Multi-Level Spins
item.description:
Pay dirt theory — Adding local 𝔰𝔲(D) exchange interactions restores Heisenberg-limited spin squeezing ξ2∝1/N in multi-level spin arrays across spatial dimensions d=1,2,3 for any power-law interaction exponent α.

Grade 0.440 · 2.4σ above the day's baseline · matched “Quantum information with Rydberg atoms” · Sakshi Bahamnia, Sagar Chaudhary, Arman Duha, Thomas Bilitewski

Figure

Minimal spin squeezing parameter ξmin⁡2 and scaling exponent ν versus gap protection strength χ, showing the transition to Heisenberg scaling ξmin⁡2∝1/N in 1D, 2D, and 3D arrays.

Asks

Can gap protection enable Heisenberg-limited spin squeezing in multi-level qudit arrays with finite-range interactions?

Before

Without protection, squeezing scales as ξmin⁡2∝N−ν with ν≈1 only for α≲d/2, degrading to ν≈1/2 at α=d and ν≲0.05 for α≳3d/2.

But

Valid during early-time exponential growth regime before depletion (ni,±1≪1). Assumes periodic boundary conditions and gap-protection strength above critical threshold χ≳χc(L).

Tools

Bogoliubov spin-wave theory · Discrete truncated Wigner approximation (dTWA) · SU(3) Casimir gap protection · Schwinger boson mapping

Abstract

We demonstrate a general mechanism to generate scalable, metrologically useful entanglement in the form of generalized spin squeezing in multi-level (qudit) spin systems with power-law interactions. We demonstrate this for spin-changing dynamics, extending the physics of spin-nematic squeezing known from spinor BECs to spatially extended lattice geometries. In the absence of all-to-all connectivity, the dynamics generally suffers from leakage into non-collective finite-momentum modes, destroying Heisenberg scaling. We show that introducing local su(D) exchange interactions establishes an energy gap that protects the fully symmetric collective manifold, suppressing non-collective excitations, and achieving Heisenberg scaling ξ²∝1/N in one to three dimensions for any power-law exponent. We provide an analytical understanding of the mechanism via the analysis of the Bogoliubov excitation spectrum, and demonstrate its effectiveness via numerical simulations of the quantum many-body dynamics. Our findings more broadly apply to other spin-squeezing Hamiltonians, and directly generalize to larger internal spin dimensions. Our results provide a practical pathway towards scalable Heisenberg-limited qudit entanglement generation in experimental platforms such as arrays of (polar) molecules, magnetic atoms, and Rydberg atoms realizing multi-level spin systems.

item.title: Subdimensional linear-optical quantum computation: from qudit resource states to qubit quantum computation
item.description:
Pay dirt new method — 2D qubit cluster states generated from 5-qudit 1D cluster states using pairwise fusion gates and adaptive single-qudit measurements, achieving fusion success probability 1−1/d without ancilla photons.

Grade 0.435 · 2.3σ above the day's baseline · matched “Long-distance quantum communication with atomic ensembles and linear optics” · Tomohiro Yamazaki

Figure

Percolation loss threshold plotted against qudit dimension d for various ancilla parameters k and k′. Shows loss tolerance increasing with d and saturating for large d.

Asks

Whether universal quantum computation can be performed using pairwise fusion gates on qudits while maintaining the boosted fusion success probability 1−1/d.

Before

Standard linear-optical fusion success probability was 50% without ancillae, or up to 75% requiring Bell state or single-photon ancillae.

But

Loss tolerance saturates at large d because pairwise fusion gates boost fusion probability but require successful single-qudit measurements; loss of photons representing graph vertices neglected in percolation model.

Tools

subspace ZX calculus · pairwise fusion gates (PFG) · connecting and merging measurements · percolation threshold simulations

Abstract

In this paper, we propose a linear-optical quantum computation scheme that starts from high-dimensionally entangled qudits but performs quantum computation on qubits defined in their subspaces. This approach enables us to increase the success probability of linear-optical fusions from 50% to 1-1/d for qudits of dimension d without relying on existing approaches using ancilla photons and quantum codes. In particular, we show that a 2D cluster state of qubits can be generated from 5-qudit 1D cluster states using pairwise fusion gates while preserving their boosted success probability. We numerically demonstrate that this approach can improve the loss tolerance of a percolation-based scheme while keeping the photon number per resource state constant.

item.title: Single-photon addition to multimode quantum fields at telecom wavelengths using lithium niobate and its doped variants
item.description:
Pay dirt theory — Collinear type-II PDC enables mode-selective single-photon addition in 5% MgO:LN at 1556 nm for temperatures between 0∘C and 15∘C (K=1.003 at 15∘C), whereas noncollinear type-I PDC enables single-photon addition with Schmidt number K=1.00002 in 2% ZnO:LN.

Grade 0.424 · 2.1σ above the day's baseline · matched “cavity QED, atom-photon interfaces and quantum networks” · Naveen V, Nicolas Treps, Raghavan G, Valentina Parigi, Srinivasan K

Figure

Phase-matching and group-velocity matching angles versus pump wavelength in 5% MgO:LN at 15∘C. The intersection at λ=778.32 nm indicates simultaneous phase-matching and group-velocity matching for mode-selective photon addition at 1556 nm.

Asks

Which phase-matching and group-velocity matching conditions allow spectro-temporal single-photon addition and mode-selective addition to multimode quantum fields at telecom wavelengths using lithium niobate and its doped variants?

Before

Mode-selective addition was known to be impossible in congruently grown bulk lithium niobate at room temperature because phase-matching and group-velocity matching cannot coincide.

But

Numerical simulations based on bulk crystal Sellmeier fits; requires cryogenic/sub-ambient cooling down to 0∘C to 15∘C for type-II mode selectivity.

Tools

Collinear type-II parametric down-conversion · Noncollinear type-I parametric down-conversion · Joint spectral amplitude Schmidt decomposition · Sellmeier equations for LN, MgO:LN, and ZnO:LN

Abstract

Multimode spectro-temporal non-Gaussian quantum states of light play a crucial role in continuous-variable quantum information processing. In particular, the non-Gaussian quantum states generated through a single-photon addition (SPA) to multimode quantum fields at telecommunication wavelengths constitute a useful resource for quantum technologies. We present a detailed theoretical analysis and numerical simulations of single-photon addition (SPA) and mode-selective single-photon addition (MSSPA) to a multimode quantum field at telecommunication wavelengths. The analysis is performed for congruently grown lithium niobate (LN), 5% MgO-doped lithium niobate (MgO:LN) and various concentrations of ZnO-doped lithium niobate (ZnO:LN) bulk crystals. We investigate MSSPA using type-II parametric down-conversion (PDC) and SPA using the type-I PDC processes. We further present spectro-temporal mode-selective SPA at the telecom wavelength using 5% MgO:LN for temperatures ranging from 0^∘ C to 15^∘ C. In addition, we perform simulations to investigate SPA based on the noncollinear type-I PDC configuration. These theoretical results identify optimal experimental conditions and phase-matching parameters to achieve SPA and mode-selective SPA for LN-based crystals, providing a potential platform for non-Gaussian quantum state engineering at telecommunication wavelengths, mainly at 1550 nm.

item.title: Design Automation for Gray-Code Quantum Read-Only Memory
item.description:
Pay dirt new method — Gray-code quantum read-only memory (GQROM) and its electronic design automation (EDA) flow minimize state transition complexity by restricting consecutive address differences to a single bit.

Grade 0.417 · 2.0σ above the day's baseline · matched “trapped-ion gates, shuttling and QCCD architectures” · Hao-Yu Lu, Yu-Ting Kao, Yeong-Jar Chang, Chao-Hung Wang, Darsen D. Lu

Asks

How to design an automated, low-overhead quantum read-only memory architecture for loading classical data into quantum circuits?

But

Validated in simulation via Qiskit platform.

Tools

Gray code encoding · Electronic design automation (EDA) flow · Qiskit platform · Quantum read-only memory (QROM)

Abstract

We propose a programmable quantum read-only memory based on Gray code encoding, termed GQROM, designed to efficiently load classical data into quantum circuits. This architecture mitigates critical bottlenecks in near-term quantum computing by reducing initialization overhead and gate-induced errors. By utilizing Gray code, in which consecutive addresses differ by only a single bit, GQROM minimizes state transition complexity. We demonstrate the architecture's flexibility in accessing targeted data through initial-state modification. The entire design, including a systematic EDA flow, was implemented and validated on the Qiskit platform, confirming its practical feasibility. These results underscore GQROM's potential as a scalable and hardware-friendly solution for efficient state preparation in quantum circuits.

item.title: Beyond Pure Dephasing: Quantum Error Correction in Single Molecules Requires Multiple Spins
item.description:
Pay dirt new method — Two-level error-correcting encoding combines embedded dephasing correction in S−𝓈 molecular spin dimers with an outer multi-qubit code, bypassing the loss of transferred coherence in anharmonic qudits.

Grade 0.417 · 2.0σ above the day's baseline · matched “Quantum information with Rydberg atoms” · Matteo Mezzadri, Silvia Macedonio, Luca Lepori, Emilio Macaluso, Francesco Albarelli, Richard E. P. Winpenny, Alessandro Chiesa, Stefano Carretta1

Figure

Entanglement infidelity Perr of planar logical rotations versus dephasing time T2 for embedded S=3/2 and S=7/2 units at different relaxation times T1, compared against bare spin-1/2 qubits.

Asks

How can fault-tolerant quantum error correction handle both diagonal dephasing and off-diagonal relaxation errors in single-molecule spin architectures?

But

Simulated under Markovian secular spin-bath dynamics at Bz=0.35 T; assumes ideal syndrome measurement and two-qubit gates on the outer code; inter-molecule entanglement mechanisms not implemented.

Tools

Redfield master equation · Knill–Laflamme conditions · Pauli twirling approximation · Steane [[7,1,3]] code · Star-shaped multi-spin clusters

Abstract

We propose multi-spin molecules as a viable architecture for fault-tolerant quantum computing. To this aim, we introduce a correction protocol handling both diagonal and off-diagonal errors, typically associated with dephasing and relaxation. The scheme is based on a hybrid encoding which combines dephasing-tolerant units suppressing the leading pure dephasing error into a multi-spin molecule implementing a multi-qubit code for residual off-diagonal errors. Our proposal leverages peculiar properties of molecular spins, i.e. the strong hierarchy between different errors and the possibility to engineer multi-spin molecules at the synthetic level. Moreover, it addresses the important issue of the loss of coherences in anharmonic systems subject to off-diagonal errors, which hampers their correction at the single spin level. Thanks to the huge suppression of dephasing by the first-level code, we numerically demonstrate the potential performance of this strategy even with a limited number of spins per logical unit.

item.title: Two-body control of noiseless subsystems with mixed SU(3) representations lifts teleportation above the classical fidelity limit
item.description:
Worth a look new result — Adjacent exchanges and one singlet-projector interaction between fundamental and dual qutrits generate all special unitary gates independently across all noiseless subsystems for any r,s≥1. For four-qutrit encoded teleportation under correlated Weyl noise, logical fidelity exceeds the classical bound 1/2 while unencoded teleportation is entanglement breaking.

Grade 0.404 · 1.8σ above the day's baseline · matched “Long-distance quantum communication with atomic ensembles and linear optics” · Otavio A. D. Molitor, Sergii Strelchuk, Michał Studziński

Figure

Teleportation fidelity plotted against transmission noise parameter. Identifies the noise interval where unencoded teleportation drops below the entanglement-breaking threshold while encoded teleportation stays above the classical fidelity bound of 1/2.

Asks

Can two-body symmetry-preserving interactions provide independent logical control across a mixed register of fundamental and dual qutrits without extra initialized ancillas?

Before

Fundamental-qutrit registers required three-body interactions for semi-universality, or two-body interactions using six ancillas (Hulse et al. 2021).

But

Pure and mixed tensor SU(3) collective noise only; gate sequence synthesis algorithm not provided; requires retaining trials where all 4 (or 5) qutrits arrive; diamond-norm perturbation bounds assume input-independent survival probabilities.

Tools

walled Brauer algebra · Lie-algebra control theory · mixed Schur-Weyl duality · correlated Weyl noise channel model · numerical pulse sequence optimization

Abstract

Collective noise can leave degrees of freedom unaffected, allowing them to store quantum information. Processing this information also requires physically available logical gates. We consider r fundamental qutrits transforming under U∈SU(3) and s dual qutrits transforming under its complex conjugate overlineU, with collective action R_(r,s)(U)=U^(⊗r)⊗overlineU^(⊗s). Using the image of the walled Brauer algebra and Lie-algebra arguments, we show that adjacent exchanges within each qutrit type and one singlet-projector interaction between the two types generate any independently chosen family of special unitary gates on the noiseless subsystems by a finite pulse sequence, for every r,s≥1. This establishes semi-universality of this system. We illustrate the result with a numerically optimised sequence of 24 pulses for three fundamental qutrits and one dual qutrit. We then use the encoding and available logical corrections for qutrit teleportation under correlated Weyl noise. Under explicit assumptions on channel composition and which trials are retained, and allowing for baseline implementation errors, we identify noise ranges in which encoded teleportation exceeds the classical fidelity bound of 1/2, while the unencoded teleportation channel is entanglement breaking. We analyse fidelity on accepted trials separately from the transmission costs of the additional physical qutrits.

item.title: Chiral Vacuum Engineering of Quantum Hall Matter
item.description:
Worth a look theory — Coupling a 2DEG to a chiral cavity isolates resonant from antiresonant vacuum interactions, yielding a handedness-dependent correction to Hall resistivity ρxy(s)=h/(νe2)−sm∗γ2D/(n2De2ωcav2) and an unsqueezed or two-mode squeezed ground state for co- or counter-rotating modes.

Grade 0.404 · 1.8σ above the day's baseline · matched “Quantum information with Rydberg atoms” · Kiran M. Kulkarni, Andrey Baydin, Motoaki Bamba, Junichiro Kono, Ceren B. Dag, Vasil Rokaj

Figure

Polariton eigenspectra, longitudinal resistivity, and Hall resistivity versus magnetic field B for counter-rotating (CRI) and co-rotating (CRA) chiral cavity modes, showing mode crossing versus anticrossing and handedness-dependent Hall corrections.

Asks

How does a circularly polarized, time-reversal-symmetry-breaking chiral cavity vacuum modify the polariton spectrum, ground state, and DC magnetotransport of a two-dimensional electron gas?

Before

In achiral or linearly polarized cavities, Hall resistivity is immune to polariton broadening and light-matter coupling at zero temperature, satisfying ρxyach=h/(νe2).

But

Spatially uniform cavity field (Kohn's theorem center-of-mass coupling), leading order in polariton broadening γ, zero temperature.

Tools

Pauli-Fierz Hamiltonian · Hopfield-Bogoliubov diagonalization · SU(2) and SU(1,1) algebraic symmetries · Drude-type DC transport inversion

Abstract

We reveal that a chiral cavity distinguishes the resonant and antiresonant interactions between a two-dimensional electron gas and the cavity vacuum. For co-rotating helicities, the modes anticross, exhibiting vacuum Rabi splitting, and retain a bare vacuum ground state. For counter-rotating helicities, the modes cross, acquiring vacuum-mediated energy shifts and a two-mode squeezed ground state. We trace the origin of these observations to the SU(2) and SU(1,1) symmetries of the respective Hamiltonians and present their spectroscopic signatures in chiral photonic crystal cavities. We further predict that cavity chirality produces a handedness-dependent correction to Hall resistivity at finite polariton broadening, while such a correction is not present in an achiral cavity. For the longitudinal resistivity, we find an asymmetric response of the Shubnikov--de Haas oscillations for the different helicities. Finally, we present an experimentally accessible route for detecting the squeezed ground state through current fluctuations. Parameters based on a recently demonstrated terahertz chiral cavity place these effects within experimental reach.
